verses.text: Let me sing a song for the one I love, a song about his vineyard. My loved one had a vineyard on a very fertile hill.

He dug it up and cleared out the stones, and planted it with the best vines. He built a watchtower in the middle of it and cut out a winepress in it. He expected it to produce good grapes, but it produced only wild, sour grapes.
"Now, people of Jerusalem and people of Judah, please judge between me and my vineyard.
What more could I have done for my vineyard that I have not done? When I expected good grapes, why did it produce only sour ones?
Now I will tell you what I am going to do to my vineyard. I will take away its hedge, and it will be eaten up. I will break down its wall, and it will be trampled.
I will make it a wasteland. It will not be trimmed or dug, and briers and thorns will grow there. I will also command the clouds not to send rain on it."

The vineyard of the LORD of Armies is the house of Israel, and the people of Judah are the garden he delighted in. He looked for justice, but saw cruelty. He looked for righteousness, but heard cries of distress.
How terrible for those who keep buying house after house and field after field, until there is no room left for anyone, and you live alone in the land!
The LORD of Armies said this in my hearing: "Surely many houses will be left empty, even great and beautiful houses, with no one living in them.
Ten acres of vineyard will produce only one bath of wine, and a homer of seed will produce only an ephah of grain."
How terrible for those who get up early in the morning to chase after strong drink, who stay up late at night until wine sets them on fire!
They have harps, lyres, tambourines, flutes, and wine at their feasts, but they do not respect what the LORD is doing. They do not think about the work of his hands.
So my people will be taken away as captives because they do not understand. Their important people will starve, and the crowds will be dried up with thirst.
So the grave has made its appetite larger and opened its mouth wide without limit. The glory of Jerusalem, its crowds, its noise, and all who party in it will go down into it.
So people will be brought low, and everyone will be humbled, and the eyes of the proud will look down.
But the LORD of Armies will be lifted high by his justice, and the holy God will show himself holy by his righteousness.
Then lambs will feed there as in their own pasture, and strangers will eat among the ruins of the rich.
How terrible for those who drag their sin along with ropes of lies, and pull wickedness behind them as if with cart ropes!
They say, "Let God hurry up and do his work quickly so we can see it! Let the plan of the Holy One of Israel come near and happen, so we will know it!"
How terrible for those who call evil good and good evil, who make darkness light and light darkness, who make bitter sweet and sweet bitter!
How terrible for those who are wise in their own eyes and clever in their own sight!
How terrible for those who are heroes at drinking wine and champions at mixing strong drinks,
who let the guilty go free for a bribe, and take away justice from the innocent!

So, as fire eats up straw and dry grass sinks down in the flames, their roots will rot and their flowers will blow away like dust. For they have rejected the teaching of the LORD of Armies and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.

That is why the LORD's anger burns against his people. He has raised his hand against them and struck them down. The mountains shake, and dead bodies lie like garbage in the streets. Even after all this, his anger has not turned away. His hand is still raised to strike.
He will raise a flag for the nations far away. He will whistle for them from the ends of the earth. Look, they are coming quickly and swiftly!
None of them will get tired or stumble. None of them will doze or sleep. Not a belt will come loose, and not a sandal strap will break.
Their arrows are sharp, and all their bows are ready. Their horses' hooves are hard as flint, and their chariot wheels spin like a whirlwind.
They roar like a lioness. They roar like young lions. They growl as they grab their prey and carry it off, and no one can rescue it.
On that day they will roar over Judah like the roaring of the sea. If anyone looks at the land, they will see only darkness and trouble. Even the light will be darkened by the clouds.
